newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Zaire envoy restates conditions for peace.
newsitem.headline: Zaire envoy restates conditions for peace.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko's nephew and chief security adviser Ngbanda Nzambo Ko Ayumba said in a radio interview on Thursday that Zaire's government stuck by its conditions for talks to end its civil war.
Ngbanda told Radio France International in an interview from Cape Town that there had "never been any question" of a meeting there between a member of Zaire's government and the rebels.
"I simply note that this morning a South African government statement specified that there was no plan for a meeting between a member of the government of Zaire and the rebels," he said.

South African President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday his country would try to bring the two sides together in Cape Town on Thursday. A spokesman for Mandela said the peace initiative was on track but South Africa put a lid on all news.

"For us there are conditions, we want first of all the real people behind this aggression to show their goodwill and respect the decisions of the Security Council," he said, referring for a U.N. call for all foreign forces to withdraw.

"We are being attacked by three neighbouring countries and we demand that the three neighbouring countries pull out their soldiers and let Zaireans find a solution to their internal problems," he added.
